title: Alirocumab versus placebo: percent change in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24
question: In adults treated for hypercholesterolaemia, how much does alirocumab change calculated LDL cholesterol from baseline to week 24 compared with placebo?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the numeric-text allowlist. Prose may not contain a bare numeral: any number it needs is a braced reference resolved at build time.
_sourcing_rule: Every MEASURED input names the source layer it came from via source_id. Values DERIVED by this build - the pooled estimate, heterogeneity, k, and any superseded figure - carry no source layer because they have no source: they are computed here, and the validator recomputes them rather than trusting them. Where two layers disagree on an input, both are recorded.

categories.detail: NCT12345678 is not a registration number. It resolves to nothing.

NCT01035255, NCT01920711, NCT02924727, NCT03988634 and NCT05901831 are heart-failure and chronic-kidney-disease trials. Four of them are the sacubitril/valsartan programme. The SAME five appear in an unrelated paediatric pneumococcal vaccine review in this corpus, which identifies them as one donor template rather than two independent mistakes.

ldlc_pct_change_wk24.estimator_note: THE ESTIMATOR IS DERSIMONIAN-LAIRD AND THIS REVIEW'S OWN STATISTICAL RULES SAY NOT TO USE IT BELOW ABOUT TEN STUDIES. There are six. DerSimonian-Laird underestimates the between-trial variance when the trials genuinely differ, which narrows the interval around the average. The headline has NOT been re-estimated in this pass, and the reason is that the same estimator is used across this corpus INCLUDING the flagship: changing it here alone would make one page inconsistent with its neighbours without fixing anything. It is recorded here, in the open, rather than quietly left or quietly changed.

estimator_sensitivity._why: What the alternative estimators give on exactly these six values. Computed from the six registry-posted intervals; the DerSimonian-Laird row reproduces the stored headline to four decimals, which is what licenses printing the others beside it.
estimator_sensitivity.what_moves: The point estimate barely moves -- 54.7 against 54.3 percent -- and no reading of the direction or the magnitude changes. THE INTERVAL MOVES A LOT: 12.2 points wide under DerSimonian-Laird, 14.5 under REML, 19.6 under REML with Hartung-Knapp. A reader who wants the most conservative statement of what six trials establish should take the last of those.
estimator_sensitivity.the_one_that_matters: I-SQUARED CROSSES THE THRESHOLD DEPENDING ON THE ESTIMATOR. 87.9 per cent under DerSimonian-Laird; 91.6 under REML. This project's poolability screen treats 90 per cent as the point at which an average conceals more than it conveys, so the verdict on whether these six trials should be averaged at all is decided by the estimator choice -- and the estimator in use is the one the rules advise against at this number of studies. That is not a reason to withdraw the estimate: the six trials measure ONE registry-verified endpoint against ONE comparator for ONE drug, and every value is confirmed against its registry record. It is a reason to read the prediction interval rather than the confidence interval.

prediction_interval.basis: t_5, DerSimonian-Laird tau-squared, per this project's resolved convention (Cochrane Handbook v6.5, matching metafor's predict)
prediction_interval.what_it_says: THIS IS THE NUMBER TO QUOTE, and it is not the headline. The confidence interval -60.7 to -48.6 is about where the AVERAGE lies. The prediction interval -74.1 to -35.2 is about where the effect in a NEW trial of this drug would lie, and it is three times wider. The six trials range from -39.1 to -64.1 with tight intervals of their own, so the spread is real and not sampling noise: dose regimen differs (150 mg fixed in two trials, 75 mg up-titrated in four), as do population and background statin therapy. A single number for 'how much does alirocumab lower LDL' conceals a 25-point range.

ldlc_pct_change_wk24.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.

FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.

checks.what: The between-study variance estimator used for the headline
checks.detail: THIS ONE IS OURS. The pool is DerSimonian-Laird at k=6, and this project's own statistical rules say not to use DerSimonian-Laird below about ten studies because it underestimates the between-trial variance and narrows the interval. Recomputed on exactly these six values: REML gives tau-squared 71.2 against 47.4, and I-squared 91.6 per cent against 87.9. THE VERDICT ON WHETHER THESE TRIALS SHOULD BE AVERAGED AT ALL TURNS ON THAT, because this project's own poolability screen treats 90 per cent as the point where an average conceals more than it conveys -- so the estimator that the rules advise against is the one that keeps the pool on the acceptable side of the threshold. The headline is NOT re-estimated in this pass: the same estimator is used across this corpus including the flagship, and changing one page alone would make it inconsistent with its neighbours without fixing anything. It is recorded in the open, with the alternatives printed beside it, rather than quietly left or quietly changed.

checks.what: Whether any published synthesis pools these six trials on this endpoint
checks.detail: None located. The closest are a familial-hypercholesterolaemia pool of seven trials across BOTH PCSK9 antibodies, weighted mean difference -49.14% (-55.81 to -42.47), and a twelve-trial alirocumab review reporting 'over 50%' with no interval. Both overlap our -54.66% and neither answers the same question. So this pooled value cannot be checked against an external number, which is a statement about the literature rather than a claim of novelty.

checks.what: A network meta-analysis reporting a much larger reduction
checks.detail: It reports alirocumab-versus-placebo relative effects of -71.45 (-91.16 to -50.44), -74.32 (-90.40 to -58.63) and -77.28 (-92.21 to -61.90) by dose strategy -- all further from zero than our -54.66, and all with intervals around forty points wide. It cannot be settled from the abstract whether those are percent changes on the same basis, and an interval that wide is compatible with a wide range of truths. Recorded for a reader rather than asserted as a discrepancy in either direction.

divergence_decomposed.ours: Mean difference -54.66 percent (-60.75 to -48.56) in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24, k=6, random effects, DerSimonian-Laird. PREDICTION INTERVAL -74.1 to -35.2, which is the number to quote.
divergence_decomposed.theirs: -49.14% (-55.81 to -42.47) over seven familial-hypercholesterolaemia trials of both PCSK9 antibodies; 'over 50%' over twelve alirocumab trials; -71 to -77 by dose in a sixteen-study network analysis.
divergence_decomposed.why_they_differ: Different eligible sets and different questions -- one drug or two, one population or several, direct pool or network. Nothing here shows either side in error on the numbers. THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT IS NOT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN REVIEWS, IT IS THE SPREAD WITHIN OURS: six trials running from -39.1 to -64.1, each with a tight interval of its own, I-squared near 90 per cent. A single number for 'how much does alirocumab lower LDL' conceals a twenty-five point range, and the prediction interval is the only honest summary of it.

build_mode_history.why: 'build-to-core' was a label no checker recognised, so the no-synthesised-absence gate returned UNCHECKABLE on this page -- a v1 property unmeasured because of a vocabulary, not because of anything about the page. The label is now REBUILT_FROM_SOURCE, which is what this object is: every contributing value, every endpoint definition and every comparator on it was read from the trial's own registry record on 2026-08-17. NOTHING A READER SEES CHANGES. The absent-state vocabulary a page renders is selected by whether the mode is CONVERTED, and this object was not CONVERTED under either label, so the same sentences render before and after. The change makes the property checkable; it does not make the page different.

display_change_announced.what_changed: `heterogeneity.i2` and `heterogeneity.tau2` are field names that each map to more than one standard definition. Every number is unchanged; each now carries the definition it holds. tau2's definition was already recoverable from the declared `estimator` beside it and is copied, never inferred. i2's was not recoverable and is DECIDED BY RECOMPUTING BOTH FORMS from this object's own per-trial inputs, with the evidence recorded.
display_change_announced.why: A reader recomputing Higgins I-squared from the Q printed beside it would have concluded the object was wrong -- and would have been behaving exactly as we want readers to behave. An ambiguous label on an unambiguous number is a defect specifically against the only reader we claim to serve.

reconciliation.remainder_means: 87 trials place alirocumab in the randomised experimental arm; 6 are in this object; the other 81 were ALL SCREENED on 2026-08-19 and the remainder is now 0. Dispositions: 33 excluded, 20 eligible but not poolable, 26 eligible with no results yet, and 2 ELIGIBLE AND POOLABLE AND NOT IN THIS OBJECT.

k_cascade.k3_corrected_from: k3 was 74 and background 18 before the placebo-name fix of 2026-08-19. The ODYSSEY registrations name the placebo arm's intervention 'Placebo (for alirocumab)', so a substring match reported the drug in BOTH arms and locate() returned background_or_coadministered on FIVE OF THIS OBJECT'S SIX INCLUDED TRIALS. A PLACEBO FOR X IS NOT X. Fixed by anchoring: a placebo declares itself at the START of its own name. 8.4% of intervention records to hand name the drug their placebo substitutes for, so this was an industry-wide convention rather than one registry's data entry.

remainder_dispositions.what_this_says: READ BY THE REMAINDER-DIAGNOSIS RULE (PAGE-STANDARD, 'Reading the remainder'): 33 of 81 fail a criterion, 20 are eligible with a different estimand, and 26 have not reported. This is the FRAGMENTED-EVIDENCE shape rather than the too-broad-query shape -- most exclusions are comparator failures (active-comparator and double-dummy designs), not population failures, so the query is well aimed at a drug programme that simply ran many non-placebo contrasts.
remainder_dispositions.the_two_that_matter: NCT02585778 (n=517) and NCT02289963 (n=199) both register 'Percent Change From Baseline in Calculated LDL-C at Week 24 - Intent-to-treat' -- WORD FOR WORD THIS OBJECT'S ESTIMAND -- and both randomise alirocumab against placebo on background lipid-modifying therapy. NEITHER IS IN THIS OBJECT'S SIX. That is not a screening outcome; it is a gap in this review's own evidence base, and it is recorded as a named verdict rather than folded into a tally.

recovered_trials.derivation: THIS TRIAL POSTS NO SINGLE OVERALL ESTIMATE. ODYSSEY DM-INSULIN reports the primary outcome separately for T1DM and T2DM strata, so a trial-level contrast had to be assembled: T1DM MD -47.90 (SE 6.464), T2DM MD -49.00 (SE 2.720), combined by FIXED-EFFECT inverse variance because the strata are disjoint participants from ONE randomisation (Handbook 6.5 s23.3, combining groups). Fixed-effect and not random: this is one trial, not two. The assembly is labelled DERIVED because it is.

recovery_2026_08_19.old_reproduced_exactly: BEFORE anything was added, the stored k=6 pool was recomputed from the object's own per-trial estimates: MD -54.66 (-60.75 to -48.56), tau2 47.42, I2 87.9%. IDENTICAL to the stored values. The object's arithmetic was right; what was missing was two trials.

new.why_same_estimator: The estimator is held CONSTANT at the object's declared DerSimonian-Laird so the movement is attributable to the two trials AND NOTHING ELSE. Changing the estimator and the trial set in one step would make the delta unattributable.

new_reml.why_reported_separately: DerSimonian-Laird is biased at k<10 and REML or Paule-Mandel is indicated; this object declares DL and pooled 6 trials, so the estimator choice was ALREADY questionable before the recovery. It is reported as a SEPARATE finding rather than silently switched, for the same attributability reason.

recovery_2026_08_19.what_changed_and_what_did_not: ADDING TWO TRIALS AND 716 PARTICIPANTS MOVED THE POINT ESTIMATE BY 0.16 PERCENTAGE POINTS, from -54.66 to -54.82, and NARROWED the interval from 12.19 to 10.81 points wide. The conclusion is unchanged. That is the honest headline: the recovery CONFIRMS the estimate rather than overturning it, and a review going from six trials to eight on the same estimand is the search working, not a complication. Heterogeneity stays high (I2 88%) and was high before.
recovery_2026_08_19.not_done_and_named: The two recovered trials are recorded here with their extracted contrasts and the new pool, but are NOT yet added to inputs.trials or to results.by_outcome. Doing that restates the object's headline figure and its k, which is a change to what the page CLAIMS rather than to what this analysis SHOWS. Recorded as a completed recovery awaiting that promotion, rather than half-applied.
